title: A Pot Full of Wit (TE)
summary: A neighboring king demands a clay pot filled with pure wit. Birbal fulfills the impossible request using a watermelon vine. [TE]
full_text:
An emissary from a rival king arrived at the court of Emperor Akbar at Agra, presenting a sealed diplomatic scroll. The letter read:

'To His Imperial Majesty Akbar: We hear constant praise of the boundless wit overflowing in your court. As a token of friendship, we request that you send us a narrow-mouthed clay pot completely filled with pure Wit. If your court cannot deliver it within three months, you must acknowledge our superior intellect!'

The courtiers were completely baffled. 'How can anyone bottle wit?' whispered the ministers. 'Wit has no physical body; it cannot be poured like water or weighed like gold!'

Akbar turned to Birbal: 'Can you deliver a pot full of wit, Birbal?'

'Grant me three months, Your Majesty,' Birbal replied with a serene bow, 'and I shall deliver a pot brimming with undeniable wit.'

Birbal walked to his private garden and instructed his gardener to plant round watermelon seeds in rich soil. When the green vines sprouted and tiny young watermelon buds appeared, Birbal carefully placed each baby melon inside a narrow-mouthed earthenware jar without detaching it from the vine.

Day after day, the gardener watered the vines. The watermelons absorbed sunlight and water, swelling larger and larger until they completely filled the interior cavity of the narrow-mouthed clay pots!

At the end of three months, Birbal cleanly severed the vine stems. The giant, ripe watermelons were trapped firmly inside the narrow jars, with no way to remove them without smashing the clay!

Birbal brought one of the sealed pots before Akbar and the waiting foreign envoy, attaching a scroll:

'Here is your pot full of wit. You may inspect the wisdom inside, on one strict condition: the wit must be extracted without cutting the fruit, and without cracking or damaging a single shard of the clay pot! If you succeed, keep the wit. If you damage the pot, acknowledge the supreme intellect of Agra!'

The envoy looked through the narrow neck. A colossal, perfect watermelon rested snugly inside, filling every millimeter of space. To remove it without breaking the pot or cutting the melon was utterly impossible!

The envoy bowed to the marble floor in deep admiration: 'Truly, only Birbal could trap pure wisdom in clay! Your court is unmatched in all the world!'

Akbar rewarded Birbal with pearls, reminding everyone that genuine intellect cultivates solutions with quiet patience.
